for any fixed natural number $k\geq 2$, there exists a natural constant $\ell$, such that, for all $n$, there exists a graph with $O(n^{1+1/k})$ paths of length at most $k$ between every two vertices.
there are graphs on $n$ vertices with $\Omega_k(n^{\frac{1}{1+\frac{1}{k}}})$ edges and $\ell$ paths between any two vertices for all $n$ and all $k$, for some $\ell$ depending on $k$.

for every natural numbers $k, \ell \geq 1$ there exists a constant $c$ such that for every natural $n$ there is a graph $G$ with $n$ verticies and $\Omega_k(c^{\ell}n^{1 + 2/\ell})$ edges with $\leq \ell$ paths of lenght $k$ between every pair of vertices.
